text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Prime Minister Kabariti meet an envoy of the Sudanese leaderhip and the king affirms Jordan's concern that no harm be done to Sudan's security and sovereignty.

- Trade minister says that the kingdom's higher oil import bill is due to higher local consumption and steep hikes in international oil prices: says Iraq offers Jordan $300 million free oil and remaining quantities at discounted prices.

- Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz says in published remarks that the "difficult period in ties with Jordan is over", adding that he noticed in recent meetings with Jordanian officials a desire to restore ties to former closeness.
- Visting Sudanese envoy praises Jordan's stance towards his country and says that the kingdom is adopting a strategic view of the conflict.
- Jordan receives a note from the head of the World Postal Union warning about a spate of letter bombs discovered in some countries, and postal bureau issues warning of letter bombs.
- Anti-corruption bureau discovers 131 corruption cases since it was set up and 209 people sent to court on charges of forgery, fraud and smuggling.
- Japanese aid official says Tokyo granted Jordan $35.2 million of grants in 1996.
- Prime minister visits the social development ministry and attends part of the planning committee meetings.
